title: Canonical cochain ringed-pullback and coherence data
statement: For small sites with independent object and morphism sizes, use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], signed direct-sum tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the normalized module comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. For the independent site sizes, generalize the normalized comparison to the same q, q_one, natural mu and generalized pure-tensor formulas; these data exist uniquely for the geometric inverse image and actual scalar-extension presentation. The landed shared-size comparison maps fieldwise into this generalization. Its signed total is the existing direct sum of inverse ordinary comparisons. A ringed pullback presentation records the left-exact inverse-image adjunction and the algebraic lift, coefficient map, actual scalar-extension module functor on objects and maps, its right adjoint, adjunction and additivity; such module presentations exist. Its cochain comparison is the inverse of the direct-sum contraction comparison and its unit is the termwise lift of the uniquely normalized ordinary unit. IsCoherent is the naturality, actual associator, Koszul braiding, and two action-unitor equations. For a third site and composable presentations, CompositePresentation records the right-adjoint composition comparisons [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and their scalar-association normalization on every generalized inverse-image generator. Normalized composite presentations exist. Its chain comparison is the termwise adjunction conjugate. IsCompatibleWithComposition is precisely the displayed tensor/composition square.

source.place: Tags 03DA, 03CY, 03D7 and 03EL; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, homogeneous tensor construction; composition normalized by Tag 0D6D.

proof.text: Construct scalarInsertion by the sheafification unit on 1 tensor m. Naturality follows from the restriction formula for changeOfRingsMap and naturality of the sheafification unit; its section formula is definitional. Apply the fixed-insertion normalized tensorator existence theorem to assemble CanonicalRingedTensorComparison.

Prove the comparison subsingleton. The q_one equation determines q sectionwise. For the inverse tensorators, test on pure tensors of scalar-extension insertions: the tensor sheafification adjunction and two sectionwise scalar-extension adjunctions make these a detecting family. Take the universal pair Z=U(M)×U(N). Preservation of products by uInv and section evaluation provides a common generalized element lifting any pair of inverse-image sections. The two pure equations identify the images under both forward tensorators. Apply their inverses and cancel; the detection lemma gives equality of inverse tensorators. Proof irrelevance handles the remaining fields.

Transport the right-adjoint module structure through the set adjunction, then compose its proved module adjunction with the scalar-extension adjunction. Take the composite of I.modules with the explicit tensorFunctor, whose object and map equations are definitional. This left adjoint preserves colimits; preservation of binary biproducts and zero gives additivity.

Construct the ordinary unit by identifying the inverse image of the regular module with the intermediate ring, then applying scalar extension. Evaluate the right-unitor equation on pure scalar-extension generators; scalar insertion sends the unit generator to one. The tensor comparison pure formula and right-unitor formula imply the required equality. Cancel the invertible tensorator and test at the regular module to prove uniqueness.

Construct the composite algebraic inverse image and coefficient morphism. Compose the underlying set adjunctions and apply the proved module presentation and tensor-comparison theorems. The normalized scalar-composition Hom argument gives an isomorphism of left module functors. Conjugate this isomorphism to define the comparison of right module functors; conjugating back recovers the original isomorphism. For set functors use the identity right comparison; its conjugate is the identity. The scalar-composition normalization is therefore exactly the CompositePresentation generator equation.
